memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD must be tended
continually'" - Lev 24:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For the third time in four verses, the same word appears: continually.
God repeats Himself here, and repetition in Scripture is never
accidental. He is pressing something into His people.

The lamp was not to be lit occasionally, or brightly on festival days
and neglected otherwise. It was tended, refilled, trimmed, watched —
day after day, year after year.

Dear friend, that is what a spiritual life actually requires. Not a
single grand decision, but continual attention. Lamps do not maintain
themselves. Wicks need trimming. Oil runs low without announcing it.

Many of us have known seasons when our faith burned brightly and other
seasons when we drifted. Usually the drift was not caused by a dramatic
sin. It was caused by neglect — a lamp nobody tended.

Paul told Timothy to fan into flame the gift of God that was in him
(2 Tim 1:6). Jesus told His disciples to remain in Him, because apart
from Him they could do nothing (John 15:4-5).

Ask yourself honestly today: what does tending look like for me this
week? Ten minutes with an open Bible? A phone call to a friend who
prays with me? Rejoining the gathering I have slipped away from?

Tend the lamp. Do it continually.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there any part of my spiritual life I have quietly neglected?
2. What one habit would help me tend my faith consistently?
3. Am I depending on past experiences instead of present nearness to
   Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I confess the places where I have let things drift through
neglect. Help me tend my walk with You faithfully, day by ordinary day.
Amen.
